## Motivation

Independent serving instances can duplicate a large read-only Engram table in host memory. This draft proposes discussing how SGLang could fetch rows from a table shared across instances, including across nodes, while preserving the existing native paths by default.

**Please treat this as a design discussion, not a ready implementation.** We would like to discuss the provider boundary, configuration, completion semantics, failure handling, and lifecycle with the community before implementing the agreed design and marking this PR ready for review.

## Modifications

Add a default-off experimental adapter through the existing Engram lookup path, plus a proposal and validation checks. The SGLang branch includes the experimental reader, owner service, READ plans and launch instructions. Only the legacy DOCA 3.1 NIXL/GPUNETIO GPU-GET library is built separately; this is not a production-ready API. An opt-in path reuses the research reader’s 16-QP READ plan and early GPU-hash prefetch. Native serving remains the default. This draft is for design review; H20 serving measurements below are pinned to the revisions actually tested.

The historical prototype used an experimental GPU-initiated NIXL/GPUNETIO READ path with DOCA 3.1 and an older SGLang snapshot; its historical performance numbers do not measure this updated PR. [NIXL issue #2543](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/issues/2543) and [NIXL draft #2544](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/pull/2544) discuss the supporting device GET; #2544 is reference material, not a current-SDK implementation.

## Accuracy Tests

Run `python test/registered/unit/layers/test_remote_engram.py` with PyTorch installed. At the updated head, 16 targeted CPU tests passed in an existing SGLang environment, including adapter capture guards and owner lease handling. The packaged owner and reader also passed a single-node, two-GPU H20 test against real checkpoint rows for both layers (4096 selections each), with 16 QPs and graph replay; the owner drained and exited. This is not a new 1P1D performance measurement. The earlier tested draft commit `a4edaf95a27657069ac32f417e0857e926a1cf62` passed a native lookup and a single-rank H20 test reading four rows from each of two remote checkpoint layers with bitwise BF16 comparison and a TP-range check. At that earlier commit, a same-version 1P1D smoke completed on two H20 nodes: TP8/CP8 P used the remote reader with bounded replay disabled; DP8 D used a native per-node host table and DSpark. One 16K-token input produced 64 output tokens, with exact text match to the prior reference; P recorded one Mooncake KV transfer. The tuned reader also passed a 4096-selection-per-layer one-GPU comparison to real checkpoint rows, including duplicate-ID restoration and graph replay. This is functional evidence, not production accuracy qualification. In the separately measured prototype, 288 paired measured outputs matched across the native and shared arms. This is historical evidence, not validation of the code in this PR.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

For the earlier draft at commit `a4edaf95a27657069ac32f417e0857e926a1cf62` (before the main-branch update), a two-node 1P1D C8 test used 16K input, 64 output tokens, three rounds of 32 measured requests plus eight warmups per arm, the same D process and matching request sets. Median of the three per-round TTFT p50 values: Native 5159.83 ms; Shared 5204.95 ms (+0.87%). Output throughput: 94.33 versus 93.52 tok/s (-0.85%). All 96 paired inputs and output text hashes matched, with zero measured cache hits, retractions or client errors. Native uses SGLang’s per-node local CPU table; Shared uses remote per-rank READ with 16 QPs and prefetch. P restarted between arms, Shared ran first, and bounded replay was disabled; there was no per-window NIC audit. P99 and production conclusions are out of scope. The historical serving results used separately provisioned reader and owner files; this PR now includes their SGLang-side implementations. Reproduction still requires the separately built native research library.

On H20, three independent prefill groups and one decode group, with 16K input, 64 output tokens and client concurrency 24, the median of three round medians was 1632.793 ms native versus 1647.930 ms shared TTFT (+0.93%); output throughput was 834.304 versus 828.517 tokens/s (-0.69%). The logical P-side table payload was three copies versus one; this is not whole-process RSS. The measurement used synthetic prompts, a debug router, the older prototype and DOCA 3.1; P abort-submission counters were nonzero in both arms and their cause was not resolved. Further details and tail metrics are in the proposal. This historical result is not a measurement of the current branch.

### H20 adaptation on a separate optimized baseline

We also applied this research idea to the public [antgroup H20 branch](https://github.com/antgroup/sglang/tree/research/shared-engram-h20-20261031) at commit [`5058e1fe5`](https://github.com/antgroup/sglang/commit/5058e1fe5). It is based on antgroup/sglang `6e6d5d9e` and is separate from the code in this PR. The three integration files and reader Python files in that commit match the hashes of the measured source; that measurement used a separately provisioned native runtime and owner. See the branch [README](https://github.com/antgroup/sglang/blob/5058e1fe5/research/shared_engram_h20/README.md) for configuration and limitations.

On H20, 1P1D, P TP8/CP8, C8, 16K input and 64 output tokens, Native versus Shared TTFT p50 was **1554.647 vs 1553.763 ms**, measured as the median of three per-round p50 values. Each round used eight warmups and 32 measured requests. All 96 paired inputs and final-text hashes matched, with no measured cache hits, retractions or client errors. These results show comparable TTFT in this workload, not a measured Shared speedup. The shared case retains one external host-memory table and avoids a table replica in each consuming instance.

The same D process was used for both arms, but P and D ran different SGLang revisions. P was restarted and the arms ran in fixed order, so the three rounds were not independently restarted deployments; per-round p99 from 32 samples is exploratory. The H20 results do not replace the current-main measurements above or constitute an exact cross-version A/B. Broader accuracy, cancellation, lifecycle and current DOCA SDK support remain open.

A subsequent functional check on the H20 adaptation used a rebuilt library from the [public legacy NIXL research snapshot](https://github.com/foraxe/nixl/tree/b5322e46f6e686ff16bdb3afb8a1a940a64e1163/research/vllm_engram_repro). Real checkpoint rows matched in both layers; the 16-QP prefetch path checked 4096 selections per layer and replayed four graphs. In a separate two-node 1P1D canary, all eight P ranks mapped the rebuilt core, plugin and shim; one uncached 16K-input/8-output request matched the prior runtime's output text. P was restarted, while D and the existing table owner remained running. This is functional evidence only; the 1553.763 ms result above used the earlier runtime, and the existing owner was not rebuilt for this canary. [More details](https://github.com/antgroup/sglang/blob/24e9dcb16f/research/shared_engram_h20/README.md#public-runtime-integration-check).

### Review status and remaining work

The branch has been updated with upstream main, includes its SGLang-side reader and owner, and the experimental feature flag follows SGLang's typed environment-variable convention. The opt-in path now requires row264 storage and a prepared READ plan, and rejects lookup during unsupported CUDA graph capture. The updated head has not yet been rerun end to end on H20; serving figures above retain their original commit and runtime attribution.

A separate legacy-runtime owner lifecycle prototype was exercised with real H20 P/D: a controlled drain retired all 256 owner QPs associated with eight 16-lane readers. That prototype is not part of this PR or a supported current-SDK implementation. Crash recovery, lifetime guarantees and the GPU GET interface still need a community-reviewed design.

## Checklist

- [x] Update documentation with the proposal and its limitations.
- [ ] Implement and validate the community-reviewed design.
- [ ] Provide tests and reproducible benchmarks for the eventual implementation.

@@ -0,0 +1,185 @@
+# Proposal: remote shared Engram tables
+
+> Discussion draft. This branch contains an experimental adapter for an
+> legacy GPU-GET library; it is not a production feature.
+> The provider interface below is illustrative, not the implemented API.
+
+## Motivation
+
+Independent serving instances may each hold the same large, read-only Engram
+table in host memory. A shared registered table could let multiple instances
+fetch the rows needed by their own requests while keeping one backing copy. The
+goal is to reduce duplicated table memory while keeping serving overhead small.
+
+SGLang already supports GPU and CPU placements, per-node host sharing and
+several lookup strategies. This proposal concerns sharing across independent
+instances, potentially on different nodes; it should complement those existing
+paths rather than replace their defaults. Remote access itself is not novel.
+
+## Candidate integration
+
+One possible integration is an opt-in table provider behind the existing Engram
+configuration. The provider owns connection setup, row requests and completion;
+the Engram layer retains hashing, TP/CP mapping, dequantization and output shape.
+The native table provider remains the default. The following is pseudocode,
+included to make the proposed boundary reviewable rather than prescribe an API:
+
+```python
+# Illustrative only: not implemented in this branch.
+provider = open_remote_table_provider(config, layer_id, row_range)
+provider.finish_load()  # establish views before CUDA graph capture
+rows, scales = provider.fetch(indices, stream=current_stream())
+# fetch must establish completion and visibility before these values are used.
+output = dequantize_and_assemble(rows, scales, indices)
+```
+
+This needs a concrete decision on asynchronous completion and GPU visibility;
+the pseudocode does not specify whether `fetch` waits, returns a completion
+handle, or arranges a stream dependency. Configuration, error propagation,
+checkpoint identity, table ownership, cancellation, graph lifetime, and
+shutdown/drain behavior also need review. An inaccessible remote table must not
+silently return incorrect data. Fallback policy needs an explicit design, since
+readers that omit local weights cannot automatically fall back to a local table.
+
+### Experimental adapter in this draft
+
+Setting `SGLANG_EXPERIMENTAL_REMOTE_ENGRAM=1` and selecting
+`--engram-config '{"placement":"cpu","replication":"none"}'` routes
+TP-owned rows through the research adapter. The option is off by default.
+The SGLang package contains the reader, owner service, and READ-plan code. It
+requires the separately built experimental NIXL/GPUNETIO GPU-GET library from
+the prior research runtime. It currently only supports 256-wide Engram layers 1 and 14.
+The experimental path requires row264 storage, `ENGRAM_SHARED_PREFETCH=1`
+and `ENGRAM_SHARED_READ_PLAN=1` for its prepared multi-QP READ plan.
+These options require the matching native library and have not been qualified
+for all graph, cancellation, or model configurations. The native NIXL GET
+implementation remains a separate dependency.
+The experimental runtime validates checkpoint identity and registered table
+metadata. The following smoke and C8 measurements used this draft at commit
+`a4edaf95a27657069ac32f417e0857e926a1cf62`, before its later main-branch
+update; the updated head has not been remeasured. With the experimental runtime,
+one same-version H20 1P1D smoke ran
+the real model with 16K input and produced 64 output tokens matching a prior
+reference output exactly. The P used TP8/CP8, bounded replay disabled and the
+remote reader; D used DP8, a native per-node host table and DSpark. Mooncake
+handled P/D KV transfer. P recorded one KV transfer, and both P/D requests
+returned successfully. This is a single functional smoke, not a performance,
+concurrency or production qualification. That historical test used separately
+provisioned reader and owner files; this draft now includes their Python code.
+
+A subsequent paired C8 test used three rounds of 32 measured requests per arm
+with 16K input and 64 output tokens on the same two H20 nodes. The Shared P
+used 16 QPs and the experimental READ plan/prefetch; Native P used the
+per-node local CPU table available at that tested revision. Both used the same D
+process, Mooncake KV, model version, prompt sets, and bounded replay disabled. Median-of-round TTFT p50 was
+5159.83 ms Native and 5204.95 ms Shared (+0.87%); output throughput was 94.33
+and 93.52 tokens/s (-0.85%). All 96 paired input and output hashes matched,
+with zero measured cache hits, retractions or client errors. P was restarted
+between arms, Shared ran first, and no per-window NIC counter audit was made;
+the sample is not a production or p99 qualification. The 1-QP path had a
+5928.08 ms TTFT p50 in one earlier 32-request round; the combined READ plan and
+prefetch changes improved that matching-input round by 12.44%, but individual
+contributions and multi-run 1-QP variance were not isolated.
+
+### Starting the research owner and reader
+
+The Python owner and reader are included in this PR. The native library is
+separate: build the legacy DOCA 3.1 research snapshot following the [NIXL
+reproducer](https://github.com/foraxe/nixl/tree/b5322e46f6e686ff16bdb3afb8a1a940a64e1163/research/vllm_engram_repro).
+Use the matching NIXL core and GPUNETIO plugin on both nodes. This is not a
+supported current-DOCA installation. Configure the local RDMA device, GID and
+OOB interface as required by that reproducer.
+
+On the owner node, set `MODEL`, `SHIM`, `OWNER_HOST` and an empty private
+`WORK` directory for your deployment, then run:
+
+```bash
+python -m sglang.srt.engram_remote.owner \
+  --checkpoint "$MODEL" --library "$SHIM" --owner-gpu 0 \
+  --rdma-port 56001 --control-host 0.0.0.0 --advertise-host "$OWNER_HOST" \
+  --control-port 56002 --ready-file "$WORK/owner.json" \
+  --stop-file "$WORK/owner.stop" --max-pinned-gib 190 --storage-layout row264
+```
+
+The ready file contains registration metadata and remote memory keys. Transfer
+it securely to the reader node and restrict the owner control network to
+trusted peers; the research control channel is not authenticated or encrypted.
+Choose unused ports and adjust the pinned-memory budget for the checkpoint.
+Do not stop the owner while readers or their GPU work are active.
+
+On the prefill node, set `MODEL`, `SHIM` and `OWNER_READY` to the matching
+checkpoint, local native library, and securely copied ready file. In addition
+to the usual SGLang P/D configuration, set:
+
+```bash
+export SGLANG_EXPERIMENTAL_REMOTE_ENGRAM=1
+export ENGRAM_SHARED_MODEL="$MODEL" ENGRAM_SHARED_LIBRARY="$SHIM"
+export ENGRAM_SHARED_READY="$OWNER_READY" ENGRAM_SHARED_READER_PORT_BASE=56100
+export ENGRAM_SHARED_PREFETCH=1 ENGRAM_SHARED_READ_PLAN=1
+export ENGRAM_SHARED_READ_LANES=16 ENGRAM_SHARED_MAX_QUERIES=393216
+export ENGRAM_SHARED_READ_GRAPH_SIZES=393216 ENGRAM_SHARED_DEFER_LAYER14=1
+# Optional: one RDMA device name per visible GPU, comma separated.
+export ENGRAM_SHARED_READER_DEVICES="<gpu0-device>,<gpu1-device>,..."
+```
+
+Use `--engram-config '{"placement":"cpu","replication":"none"}'` for
+this experimental path. Keep the decode node on its native Engram path. These
+legacy `ENGRAM_SHARED_*` keys configure the research reader and native ABI;
+their final configuration surface is part of the design discussion. To check
+both checkpoint layers with one reader GPU, set `ENGRAM_SHARED_MAX_QUERIES=8192`
+and `ENGRAM_SHARED_READ_GRAPH_SIZES=4096`, then run:
+
+```bash
+python test/manual/engram_remote_smoke.py
+```
+
+After readers have stopped and drained, create the owner stop file and wait for
+it to exit. Failed readers can leave orphan leases; this prototype intentionally
+does not reclaim them on a timer. The older native backend can retain per-peer
+QP resources until owner exit, so repeated restarts require special care.
+
+## Research evidence and limits
+
+An external research prototype, based on SGLang commit
+`9a9ae36865e6c7c24fcbf3ce44a14b5e2945709a` and adapter commit
+`c2ba4222787820e5d46069a163b49ded95a94aee`, used GPU-initiated READs from a
+registered pinned-host table. It used an experimental NIXL/GPUNETIO path and
+DOCA 3.1; it is not an implementation of this proposal on current main. Its
+private TP/CP hooks and underlying NIXL interfaces need to be ported and
+reviewed. NIXL device-GET discussion: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/issues/2543
+and reference draft: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/nixl/pull/2544. The latter is
+not a current-SDK runnable implementation.
+
+In a paired H20 experiment, three independent TP8 prefill groups shared one
+remote table while a TP8/DP8 decode group kept its native table. P/D KV
+transport used Mooncake in both arms. With 16K input tokens, 64 output tokens,
+client concurrency 24, DSPARK block size 5 and decode CUDA graphs, three rounds
+of 96 measured requests per arm produced matching outputs for all 288 pairs.
+The median of the three round medians was 1632.793 ms native versus 1647.930 ms
+shared TTFT (+0.93%), and 834.304 versus 828.517 output tokens/s (-0.69%).
+TTFT p99 was +2.68% and TPOT p90 +5.69%; per-round samples are small and these
+are not production tail guarantees. All measured client requests completed;
+prefill abort-submission counters were nonzero in both arms and their cause
+remains unresolved.
+
+The P-side logical table payload was three copies versus one shared copy, a
+66.7% reduction. Including the unchanged D table, it was four copies versus two,
+a 50% reduction. These are logical payload counts, not measured total RSS. The
+owner still consumes pinned host memory and readers consume workspace. The

+"""Per-lookup representatives; no rows or request state survive workspace reset."""
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _representatives(
+    ids, out, table, query_list, lo, hi, S: tl.constexpr, COMPACT: tl.constexpr
+):
+    q = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    row = tl.load(ids + q).to(tl.int64)
+    representative = tl.full((), -1, tl.int64)
+    if (row >= lo) & (row < hi):
+        slot = (row * 2654435761) & (S - 1)
+        key = ((row.to(tl.uint64) + 1) << 32) | q.to(tl.uint64)
+        seen = tl.atomic_cas(
+            table + slot, tl.full((), 0, tl.uint64), key, sem="relaxed"
+        )
+        while (seen != 0) & ((seen >> 32) != (row.to(tl.uint64) + 1)):
+            slot = (slot + 1) & (S - 1)
+            seen = tl.atomic_cas(
+                table + slot, tl.full((), 0, tl.uint64), key, sem="relaxed"
+            )
+        representative = tl.where(seen == 0, q, (seen & 0xFFFFFFFF).to(tl.int64))
+        if COMPACT:
+            if seen == 0:
+                slot_out = tl.atomic_add(
+                    table + S, tl.full((), 1, tl.uint64), sem="relaxed"
+                )
+                tl.store(query_list + slot_out, q)
+    tl.store(out + q, representative)
+
+
+def workspace(n, device):
+    slots = triton.next_power_of_2(max(2, 2 * n))
+    return torch.empty(slots + 1, dtype=torch.uint64, device=device), torch.empty(
+        n, dtype=torch.int64, device=device
+    )
+
+
+def prepare(ids, lo, hi, scratch, out, query_list=None):
+    if not (
+        ids.dtype == torch.int64
+        and ids.is_cuda
+        and ids.is_contiguous()
+        and out.shape == ids.shape
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("invalid dedup IDs/output")
+    if not 0 <= lo <= hi < 2**32 or ids.numel() >= 2**32:
+        raise ValueError("dedup key/index range")
+    if scratch.numel() < 2 * ids.numel():
+        raise ValueError("dedup table capacity")
+    scratch.zero_()
+    if ids.numel():
+        _representatives[(ids.numel(),)](
+            ids,
+            out,
+            scratch,
+            query_list if query_list is not None else out,
+            lo,
+            hi,
+            S=scratch.numel() - 1,
+            COMPACT=query_list is not None,
+            num_warps=1,
+        )
+    return out

+import ctypes as C
+import uuid
+
+import torch
+
+
+class Context:
+    def __init__(self, library, gpu, port):
+        self.gpu = gpu
+        # The backend is dlopened later and must see the same host/Abseil symbols.
+        self.library = C.CDLL(str(library), mode=C.RTLD_GLOBAL)
+        lib = self.library
+        lib.engram_abi_version.restype = C.c_uint32
+        if lib.engram_abi_version() != 3:
+            raise RuntimeError("shared Engram shim/wrapper ABI mismatch")
+        lib.engram_last_error.restype = C.c_char_p
+        lib.engram_create.argtypes = [C.c_uint32, C.c_uint16, C.c_char_p]
+        lib.engram_create.restype = C.c_void_p
+        lib.engram_register.argtypes = [
+            C.c_void_p,
+            C.c_int,
+            C.POINTER(C.c_uint64),
+            C.POINTER(C.c_uint64),
+            C.c_uint32,
+        ]
+        lib.engram_metadata.argtypes = [C.c_void_p, C.c_void_p, C.c_size_t]
+        lib.engram_metadata.restype = C.c_int64
+        lib.engram_connect.argtypes = [
+            C.c_void_p,
+            C.c_void_p,
+            C.c_size_t,
+            C.POINTER(C.c_uint64),
+            C.POINTER(C.c_uint64),
+            C.c_uint32,
+            C.c_uint32,
+        ]
+        lib.engram_destroy.argtypes = [C.c_void_p]
+        lib.engram_record_consumed.argtypes = [C.c_void_p, C.c_uint64]
+        self.handle = lib.engram_create(
+            gpu, port, ("shared-engram-" + uuid.uuid4().hex).encode()
+        )
+        if not self.handle:
+            raise RuntimeError(lib.engram_last_error().decode())
+        self.buffers = []
+
+    def check(self, rc):
+        if rc < 0:
+            raise RuntimeError(self.library.engram_last_error().decode())
+        return rc
+
+    def register(self, tensors, host):
+        if self.buffers:
+            raise RuntimeError("context already has a registration")
+        if any(not t.is_contiguous() for t in tensors):
+            raise ValueError("registration tensors must be contiguous")
+        if host and any(t.is_cuda or not t.is_pinned() for t in tensors):
+            raise ValueError("owner tensors must be pinned Host allocations")
+        if not host and (len(tensors) != 1 or not tensors[0].is_cuda):
+            raise ValueError("reader requires one CUDA arena")
+        self.addresses = (C.c_uint64 * len(tensors))(*(t.data_ptr() for t in tensors))
+        self.lengths = (C.c_uint64 * len(tensors))(
+            *(t.numel() * t.element_size() for t in tensors)
+        )
+        self.check(
+            self.library.engram_register(
+                self.handle, int(host), self.addresses, self.lengths, len(tensors)
+            )
+        )
+        self.buffers = list(tensors)
+
+    def metadata(self):
+        size = self.check(self.library.engram_metadata(self.handle, None, 0))
+        out = C.create_string_buffer(size)
+        self.check(self.library.engram_metadata(self.handle, out, size))
+        return out.raw
+
+    def connect_raw(self, blob, addresses, lengths, remote_gpu):
+        if (
+            not addresses
+            or len(addresses) != len(lengths)
+            or any(n <= 0 for n in lengths)
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("invalid remote registration descriptors")
+        addr = (C.c_uint64 * len(addresses))(*addresses)
+        size = (C.c_uint64 * len(lengths))(*lengths)
+        md = C.create_string_buffer(blob)
+        self.check(
+            self.library.engram_connect(
+                self.handle, md, len(blob), addr, size, len(addresses), remote_gpu
+            )
+        )
+        self.remote_count = len(addresses)
+
+    def close(self):
+        if self.handle:
+            self.check(self.library.engram_destroy(self.handle))
+            self.handle = None
+            self.buffers.clear()
+
+    def record_consumed(self):
+        self.check(
+            self.library.engram_record_consumed(
+                self.handle, torch.cuda.current_stream(self.gpu).cuda_stream
+            )
+        )

+def _sha256(data):
+    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()

+def _safetensors_header(path):
+    """Read only the bounded safetensors header, returning parsed header/hash."""
+    with open(path, "rb") as stream:
+        prefix = stream.read(8)
+        if len(prefix) != 8:
+            raise ValueError(f"short safetensors header: {path}")
+        (length,) = struct.unpack("<Q", prefix)
+        if not 2 <= length <= MAX_HEADER_BYTES:
+            raise ValueError(f"invalid safetensors header length {length}: {path}")
+        raw = stream.read(length)
+        if len(raw) != length:
+            raise ValueError(f"truncated safetensors header: {path}")
+    header = json.loads(raw)
+    if not isinstance(header, dict):
+        raise ValueError(f"safetensors header is not an object: {path}")
+    return header, _sha256(prefix + raw), 8 + length

+def inspect_checkpoint(root):
+    """Validate config/index/selected tensor headers without reading tensor data."""
+    root = Path(root).resolve(strict=True)

+    config_bytes, index_bytes = config_path.read_bytes(), index_path.read_bytes()
+    config, index = json.loads(config_bytes), json.loads(index_bytes)
+    text_config = config.get("text_config", config)
+    rows = tuple(text_config.get("engram_num_embeddings", ()))
+    layers = tuple(text_config.get("engram_layer_ids", ()))
+    if layers != LAYERS or len(rows) != len(LAYERS):
+        raise ValueError(f"unexpected Engram config layers/rows: {layers}, {rows}")
+    if int(text_config.get("engram_head_dim", WEIGHT_COLS)) != WEIGHT_COLS:
+        raise ValueError("Engram head dimension is not 256")

+    if not isinstance(weight_map, dict):
+        raise ValueError("safetensors index has no weight_map")
+
+    specs, shard_headers = [], {}
+    for layer, row_count in zip(LAYERS, rows):
+        for kind, dtype, columns in (
+            ("weight", WEIGHT_DTYPE, WEIGHT_COLS),
+            ("scale", SCALE_DTYPE, SCALE_COLS),
+        ):
+            name = f"layers.{layer}.engram.embed.{kind}"
+            shard_name = weight_map.get(name)

+                raise ValueError(f"missing or unsafe index entry for {name}")

+                shard_headers[shard_name] = {
+                    "path": str(shard_path),
+                    "header": header,
+                    "header_sha256": header_hash,
+                    "data_start": data_start,
+                    "file_size": shard_path.stat().st_size,
+                }

+            shape = [int(row_count), columns]

+                raise ValueError(f"{name}: expected dtype {dtype}, got {tensor}")
+            if tensor.get("shape") != shape:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"{name}: expected shape {shape}, got {tensor.get('shape')}"
+                )
+            offsets = tensor.get("data_offsets")
+            size = int(row_count) * columns

+                not isinstance(offsets, list)
+                or len(offsets) != 2
+                or offsets[1] - offsets[0] != size
+                or offsets[0] < 0
+                or shard["data_start"] + offsets[1] > shard["file_size"]
+            ):
+                raise ValueError(f"{name}: invalid data_offsets {offsets}")
+            specs.append(
+                {
+                    "name": name,
+                    "layer": layer,
+                    "kind": kind,
+                    "dtype": dtype,
+                    "shape": shape,
+                    "rows": int(row_count),
+                    "columns": columns,
+                    "nbytes": size,
+                    "data_offsets": offsets,
+                    "shard": shard_name,
+                }
+            )

+    header_records = {
+        name: {"header_sha256": item["header_sha256"], "file_size": item["file_size"]}
+        for name, item in sorted(shard_headers.items())
+    }

+        "config_sha256": _sha256(config_bytes),
+        "index_sha256": _sha256(index_bytes),
+        "selected_shard_headers": header_records,
+        "tensors": [
+            {k: spec[k] for k in ("name", "dtype", "shape", "data_offsets", "shard")}
+            for spec in specs
+        ],
+    }

+        "config": config,
+        "index": index,
+        "shards": shard_headers,
+        "specs": specs,
+        "identity_material": identity_material,
+        "checkpoint_identity": "sha256:" + identity,

+def _copy_and_sample_row264(manifest, destination, chunk_bytes):

+    import numpy as np

+        raise ValueError(f"copy chunk must be in (0, {MAX_COPY_CHUNK}]")

+        by_layer.setdefault(spec["layer"], {})[spec["kind"]] = spec

+        digests = {"weight": hashlib.sha256(), "scale": hashlib.sha256()}
+        with ExitStack() as stack:
+            mappings = {}
+            for part in (weight, scale):
+                shard = manifest["shards"][part["shard"]]

+                    stream = stack.enter_context(open(shard["path"], "rb"))

+            scale_map, scale_data_start = mappings[scale["shard"]]
+            weight_start = weight_data_start + weight["data_offsets"][0]
+            scale_start = scale_data_start + scale["data_offsets"][0]
+            for row0 in range(0, rows, chunk_rows):
+                count = min(chunk_rows, rows - row0)
+                packed_offset = offset + row0 * (WEIGHT_COLS + SCALE_COLS)
+                source_weight = np.ndarray(
+                    (count, WEIGHT_COLS),
+                    dtype=np.uint8,
+                    buffer=weight_map,
+                    offset=weight_start + row0 * WEIGHT_COLS,
+                )
+                target_weight = np.ndarray(
+                    (count, WEIGHT_COLS),
+                    dtype=np.uint8,
+                    buffer=destination,
+                    offset=packed_offset,
+                    strides=(WEIGHT_COLS + SCALE_COLS, 1),
+                )
+                source_scale = np.ndarray(
+                    (count, SCALE_COLS),
+                    dtype=np.uint8,
+                    buffer=scale_map,
+                    offset=scale_start + row0 * SCALE_COLS,
+                )
+                target_scale = np.ndarray(
+                    (count, SCALE_COLS),
+                    dtype=np.uint8,
+                    buffer=destination,
+                    offset=packed_offset + WEIGHT_COLS,
+                    strides=(WEIGHT_COLS + SCALE_COLS, 1),
+                )
+                np.copyto(target_weight, source_weight, casting="no")
+                np.copyto(target_scale, source_scale, casting="no")

+                packed_row = offset + row * (WEIGHT_COLS + SCALE_COLS)
+                expected_weight = weight_map[
+                    weight_start + row * WEIGHT_COLS : weight_start
+                    + (row + 1) * WEIGHT_COLS
+                ]
+                expected_scale = scale_map[
+                    scale_start + row * SCALE_COLS : scale_start
+                    + (row + 1) * SCALE_COLS
+                ]
+                copied_weight = bytes(
+                    destination[packed_row : packed_row + WEIGHT_COLS]
+                )
+                copied_scale = bytes(
+                    destination[
+                        packed_row + WEIGHT_COLS : packed_row + WEIGHT_COLS + SCALE_COLS
+                    ]
+                )
+                if copied_weight != expected_weight or copied_scale != expected_scale:
+                    raise RuntimeError(
+                        f"row264 sampled bytes differ from checkpoint, layer={layer} row={row}"
+                    )
+                digests["weight"].update(row.to_bytes(8, "little") + expected_weight)
+                digests["scale"].update(row.to_bytes(8, "little") + expected_scale)
+
+        tables.append(
+            {
+                "name": f"layers.{layer}.engram.embed.row264",
+                "layer": layer,
+                "kind": "row264",
+                "dtype": "uint8",
+                "shape": [rows, 264],
+                "rows": rows,
+                "columns": 264,
+                "nbytes": table_bytes,
+                "offset": offset,
+                "component_layout": {
+                    "weight": {
+                        "offset": 0,
+                        "bytes_per_row": WEIGHT_COLS,
+                        "dtype": WEIGHT_DTYPE,
+                    },
+                    "scale": {
+                        "offset": WEIGHT_COLS,
+                        "bytes_per_row": SCALE_COLS,
+                        "dtype": SCALE_DTYPE,
+                    },
+                },
+            }
+        )
+        samples.append(
+            {
+                "layer": layer,
+                "rows": row_ids,
+                "weight_sample_bytes_sha256": digests["weight"].hexdigest(),
+                "scale_sample_bytes_sha256": digests["scale"].hexdigest(),
+                "exact_match": True,
+            }

+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"row264 backing size mismatch: packed={offset} allocated={len(destination)}"
+        )

+def build_owner_metadata(

+"""Small setup/drain control channel for a shared Engram owner.
+
+This protocol carries lifecycle control only. It is not on the lookup/data path.
+The caller must wait for CUDA/NIC work to complete before releasing its lease;
+these messages cannot prove GPU or network completion.

+import json
+import secrets
+import socket

+import threading
+from contextlib import AbstractContextManager

+MAX_FRAME = 64 * 1024

+class ControlError(RuntimeError):
+    """A lifecycle request was rejected or could not be completed."""
+

+def _freeze(value):
+    if isinstance(value, dict):
+        return MappingProxyType({k: _freeze(v) for k, v in value.items()})
+    if isinstance(value, list):
+        return tuple(_freeze(v) for v in value)
+    return value
+

+def _read_frame(sock):
+    data = bytearray()
+    while len(data) <= MAX_FRAME:
+        chunk = sock.recv(min(4096, MAX_FRAME + 1 - len(data)))
+        if not chunk:
+            break
+        pos = chunk.find(b"\n")
+        data.extend(chunk if pos < 0 else chunk[:pos])
+        if pos >= 0:
+            if len(data) > MAX_FRAME:
+                raise ValueError("frame too large")
+            return bytes(data)
+    if len(data) > MAX_FRAME:
+        raise ValueError("frame too large")
+    raise ValueError("unterminated frame")
+
+
+def _send(sock, obj):
+    body = json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8") + b"\n"
+    if len(body) > MAX_FRAME:
+        raise ValueError("frame too large")
+    sock.sendall(body)

+    allow_reuse_address = True
+    daemon_threads = True

+    """Serve attach/release/drain for one owner generation.

+    leases or claims that device work has completed.

+            metadata.get("checkpoint_id"), str

+        if len(encoded.encode("utf-8")) > MAX_FRAME - 256:
+            raise ValueError("metadata too large for control frame")
+        self._metadata_json = encoded
+        self.metadata = _freeze(json.loads(encoded))
+        self.generation = secrets.token_urlsafe(24)
+        self._lock = threading.RLock()
+        self._leases = set()
+        self._draining = False
+        self._closed = False

+            def handle(self):
+                try:
+                    request = json.loads(_read_frame(self.request).decode("utf-8"))
+                    if not isinstance(request, dict):
+                        raise ValueError("request must be an object")
+                    result = owner._dispatch(request)
+                    response = {"ok": True, **result}
+                except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
+                    response = {"ok": False, "error": f"invalid request: {exc}"}
+                except ControlError as exc:
+                    response = {"ok": False, "error": str(exc)}
+                try:
+                    _send(self.request, response)
+                except (OSError, ValueError):

+        self._server = _ThreadingServer((host, port), Handler)

+    def address(self):
+        return self._server.server_address
+

+

+        if request.get("generation") != self.generation:
+            raise ControlError("stale or wrong generation")
+
+    def _dispatch(self, request):
+        op = request.get("op")
+        with self._lock:
+            if self._closed:
+                raise ControlError("owner is closed")
+            self._check_generation(request)
+            if op == "status":
+                return {
+                    "generation": self.generation,
+                    "leases": len(self._leases),
+                    "draining": self._draining,
+                }
+            if op == "attach":
+                if request.get("checkpoint_id") != self.metadata["checkpoint_id"]:
+                    raise ControlError("checkpoint identity mismatch")
+                if self._draining:
+                    raise ControlError("owner is draining")
+                lease = secrets.token_urlsafe(24)
+                self._leases.add(lease)
+                return {
+                    "metadata": json.loads(self._metadata_json),
+                    "generation": self.generation,
+                    "lease": lease,
+                }
+            if op == "release":
+                lease = request.get("lease")
+                if not isinstance(lease, str) or lease not in self._leases:
+                    raise ControlError("unknown or already released lease")
+                self._leases.remove(lease)
+                return {"released": True}
+            if op == "drain":
+                self._draining = True
+                return {"draining": True, "leases": len(self._leases)}
+            raise ValueError("unknown operation")
+
+    def close(self):
+        with self._lock:
+            if self._closed:
+                return
+            self._draining = True
+            if self._leases:
+                raise ControlError(f"cannot close: {len(self._leases)} lease(s) remain")
+            self._closed = True
+        if self._thread is not None:
+            self._server.shutdown()
+        self._server.server_close()
+        if self._thread is not None:
+            self._thread.join()
+
+    def __enter__(self):
+        return self.start()
+
+    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb):
+        self.close()
+
+
+class OwnerClient:
+    """A client pinned to an expected checkpoint identity and generation."""
+
+    def __init__(self, host, port, checkpoint_id, generation, timeout=30.0):
+        self.host, self.port = host, port
+        self.checkpoint_id, self.generation = checkpoint_id, generation
+        self.timeout = timeout
+
+    def _request(self, op, **fields):
+        request = {"op": op, "generation": self.generation, **fields}
+        with socket.create_connection((self.host, self.port), self.timeout) as sock:
+            sock.settimeout(self.timeout)
+            _send(sock, request)
+            response = json.loads(_read_frame(sock).decode("utf-8"))
+        if not isinstance(response, dict) or not response.get("ok"):
+            raise ControlError(
+                response.get("error", "invalid server response")
+                if isinstance(response, dict)
+                else "invalid server response"
+            )
+        return response
+
+    def attach(self):
+        response = self._request("attach", checkpoint_id=self.checkpoint_id)
+        if (
+            response.get("generation") != self.generation
+            or response.get("metadata", {}).get("checkpoint_id") != self.checkpoint_id
+        ):

+
+    def begin_drain(self):
+        return self._request("drain")
+
+    def status(self):
+        return self._request("status")
+
+
+class Lease(AbstractContextManager):
+    """Explicit reader lease; release only after caller has drained device work."""
+
+    def __init__(self, client, token, metadata):
+        self.client, self.token = client, token
+        self.metadata = _freeze(metadata)
+        self._released = False

+    def release(self):
+        if self._released:
+            raise ControlError("lease already released")
+        # Caller obligation: synchronize/drain all CUDA/NIC operations that can
+        # access the owner table before invoking release().
+        self.client._request("release", lease=self.token)
+        self._released = True
+
+    def __enter__(self):
+        return self
+
+    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb):
+        self.release()

+"""Bit-preserving E4M3/E8M0 lookup from a contiguous264-byte row.
+
+Raw pointers allow the same consumer arithmetic for registered Host and GPU
+backing. query_order=True decodes the RDMA result at the original query slot.
+"""
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _gather(
+    base, ids, output, lo, hi, reps, QUERY_ORDER: tl.constexpr, MAPPED: tl.constexpr
+):
+    q = tl.program_id(0).to(tl.int64)
+    idx = tl.load(ids + q).to(tl.int64)
+    owned = (idx >= lo) & (idx < hi)
+    row = q if QUERY_ORDER else tl.where(owned, idx - lo, 0)
+    if MAPPED:
+        row = tl.load(reps + q, mask=owned, other=0)
+        owned = owned & (row >= 0) & (row < tl.num_programs(0))
+    byte = base.to(tl.int64).to(tl.pointer_type(tl.uint8))
+    fp8 = byte.to(tl.pointer_type(tl.float8e4nv))
+    x = tl.arange(0, 256)
+    value = tl.load(fp8 + row * 264 + x, mask=owned, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    exp = tl.load(byte + row * 264 + 256 + x // 32, mask=owned, other=0).to(tl.int32)
+    scale = (exp << 23).to(tl.float32, bitcast=True)
+    scale = tl.where(exp == 0, 2.0**-127, scale)
+    result = tl.where(owned, value * scale, 0.0)
+    tl.store(output + q * 256 + x, result.to(tl.bfloat16))
+
+
+def gather_row264(
+    pointer,
+    ids,
+    output,
+    row_lo=0,
+    row_hi=2**62,
+    query_order=False,
+    representatives=None,
+):
+    if ids.dtype != torch.int64 or not ids.is_cuda or not ids.is_contiguous():
+        raise ValueError("row264 IDs must be contiguous CUDA int64")
+    if (
+        output.dtype != torch.bfloat16
+        or not output.is_contiguous()
+        or output.numel() != ids.numel() * 256
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("row264 output must be contiguous BF16 with256 columns")
+    if representatives is not None and (
+        representatives.dtype != torch.int64
+        or representatives.shape != ids.shape
+        or representatives.device != ids.device
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("invalid mapped row indices")
+    if ids.numel():
+        _gather[(ids.numel(),)](
+            pointer,
+            ids,
+            output,
+            row_lo,
+            row_hi,
+            representatives if representatives is not None else ids,
+            QUERY_ORDER=query_order,
+            MAPPED=representatives is not None,
+            num_warps=4,
+        )
+    return output

+"""Experimental adapter for the external shared-Engram research runtime.
+
+This adapter is opt-in and is not a supported NIXL integration. Its reader and
+owner live in SGLang; the native GPU-GET library is a separate research build.
+The reader owns registered scratch until GPU work retires.
+"""
+
+import os
+
+import torch
+
+_runtime = None
+
+
+def prepare_forward(cp_extend: bool):
+    if _runtime is None or not _runtime.prefetch_enabled:
+        raise RuntimeError("remote Engram prefetch runtime is not initialized")
+    _runtime.start_forward(cp_extend)
+
+
+def prefetch_full_hash(hash_ids, local_rows: int, cp_size: int):
+    if _runtime is None:
+        raise RuntimeError("remote Engram reader has not finished loading")
+    _runtime.begin_prefetch(hash_ids, local_rows, cp_size)
+
+
+class RemoteEngramTable:
+    def __init__(self, num_embeddings: int, dim: int, layer_id: int):
+        if dim != 256 or layer_id not in (1, 14):
+            raise ValueError("research remote Engram supports 256-wide layers 1 and 14")
+        self.num_embeddings = num_embeddings
+        self.dim = dim
+        self.layer_id = layer_id
+        self.loaded = set()
+        self.runtime = None
+
+    def check_weight(self, param, loaded_weight, weight):
+        kind = "weight" if param is weight else "scale"
+        width = self.dim if kind == "weight" else self.dim // 32
+        if tuple(loaded_weight.shape) != (self.num_embeddings, width):
+            raise ValueError("remote Engram checkpoint tensor shape mismatch")
+        if loaded_weight.dtype != param.dtype:
+            raise ValueError("remote Engram checkpoint tensor dtype mismatch")
+        self.loaded.add(kind)
+
+    def finish_load(self, row_start: int, rows: int):
+        global _runtime
+        if self.loaded != {"weight", "scale"}:
+            raise RuntimeError("remote Engram checkpoint parameters not loaded")
+        if _runtime is None:
+            from sglang.srt.engram_remote.runtime import ReaderRuntime
+
+            _runtime = ReaderRuntime()
+        self.runtime = _runtime
+        layer_index = (1, 14).index(self.layer_id)
+        expected = (self.num_embeddings * 264,)
+        actual = self.runtime.metadata["lengths"][layer_index : layer_index + 1]
+        if tuple(actual) != expected:
+            raise ValueError("remote Engram table size mismatch")
+        self.runtime.ranges[self.layer_id] = (row_start, row_start + rows)
+        if os.environ.get("ENGRAM_SHARED_READ_PLAN") == "1" and set(
+            self.runtime.ranges
+        ) == {1, 14}:
+            with torch.cuda.stream(self.runtime.comm_stream):
+                self.runtime.context.prime(
+                    self.runtime.ranges,
+                    self.runtime.p_off,
+                    self.runtime.dump,
+                    self.runtime.layer_stats,
+                )
+
+    def lookup(self, indices, row_start: int, rows: int, new_rows):
+        if self.runtime is None:
+            raise RuntimeError("remote Engram reader has not finished loading")
+        out = new_rows(indices)
+        if not indices.numel():
+            return out
+        if torch.cuda.is_current_stream_capturing():
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "remote Engram QP prefetch is unsupported during CUDA graph capture"
+            )
+        ids, weight, _ = self.runtime.fetch(
+            indices, self.layer_id, row_start, row_start + rows
+        )
+        from sglang.srt.engram_remote.row264_kernels import gather_row264
+
+        representatives = self.runtime.context.representatives(
+            (1, 14).index(self.layer_id)
+        )
+        gather_row264(
+            weight.data_ptr(),
+            ids,
+            out.view(-1, self.dim),
+            row_start,
+            row_start + rows,
+            query_order=True,
+            representatives=representatives,
+        )
+        self.runtime.record_consumed(self.layer_id)
+        return out
+
+    def after_reduction(self):
+        if (
+            self.layer_id == 1
+            and self.runtime.prefetch_enabled
+            and self.runtime.defer_layer14
+        ):
+            self.runtime.issue_prefetch_layer(14)

+"""Validate packaged remote Engram QP16 prefetch against checkpoint rows.
+
+Start the experimental owner first and set the ENGRAM_SHARED_* configuration
+shown in remote_engram_proposal.md. This test needs one assigned CUDA GPU,
+access to the same checkpoint, and the matching legacy native library.
+"""
+
+import json
+import os
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+from safetensors import safe_open
+
+from sglang.srt.layers import remote_engram
+
+
+def main():
+    model = Path(os.environ["ENGRAM_SHARED_MODEL"])
+    index = json.loads((model / "model.safetensors.index.json").read_text())[
+        "weight_map"
+    ]
+    config = json.loads((model / "config.json").read_text())
+    config = config.get("text_config", config)
+    layers = (1, 14)
+    tables = []
+    reader = None
+    try:
+        for layer, count in zip(layers, config["engram_num_embeddings"]):
+            table = remote_engram.RemoteEngramTable(int(count), 256, layer)
+            weight = torch.empty((0, 256), dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+            scale = torch.empty((0, 8), dtype=torch.float8_e8m0fnu)
+            table.check_weight(
+                weight,
+                SimpleNamespace(shape=(int(count), 256), dtype=weight.dtype),
+                weight,
+            )
+            table.check_weight(
+                scale, SimpleNamespace(shape=(int(count), 8), dtype=scale.dtype), weight
+            )
+            table.finish_load(0, int(count))
+            tables.append(table)
+            reader = table.runtime
+        if not reader.prefetch_enabled or not hasattr(reader.context, "graph_sizes"):
+            raise RuntimeError("enable prefetch and the prepared READ plan")
+        values = [0, 1, 1234, 8191]
+        base = torch.tensor(values, dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda")
+        full = base[torch.arange(256 * 2 * 16, device="cuda").remainder(4)].view(
+            256, 2, 16
+        )
+        remote_engram.prepare_forward(True)
+        remote_engram.prefetch_full_hash(full, 64, 4)
+        ordered = torch.cat([full[rank::4] for rank in range(4)], dim=0)
+        references = []
+        for layer_index, layer in enumerate(layers):
+            count = int(config["engram_num_embeddings"][layer_index])
+            ids = ordered[:, layer_index, :].contiguous().view(-1)
+            output = tables[layer_index].lookup(
+                ids,
+                0,
+                count,
+                lambda query: torch.empty(
+                    (query.numel(), 256), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda"
+                ),
+            )
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            key_w = f"layers.{layer}.engram.embed.weight"
+            key_s = f"layers.{layer}.engram.embed.scale"
+            with safe_open(
+                str(model / index[key_w]), framework="pt", device="cpu"
+            ) as f:
+                weights = torch.cat(
+                    [f.get_slice(key_w)[i : i + 1] for i in values]
+                ).float()
+                scales = torch.cat(
+                    [f.get_slice(key_s)[i : i + 1] for i in values]
+                ).view(torch.uint8)
+            expected = (
+                weights
+                * torch.exp2(scales.int().float() - 127).repeat_interleave(32, 1)
+                + 0.0
+            ).to(torch.bfloat16)
+            references.append(expected)
+            ids_cpu = ids.cpu()
+            actual = output.cpu()
+            for i, value in enumerate(values):
+                selected = actual[ids_cpu == value].contiguous().view(torch.int16)
+                reference = (
+                    expected[i]
+                    .expand(selected.shape[0], -1)
+                    .contiguous()
+                    .view(torch.int16)
+                )
+                assert torch.equal(selected, reference), (layer, value)
+            print(f"PASS layer={layer} selections={ids.numel()}", flush=True)
+        # Non-CP health requests use a single lane of the same prepared plan.
+        remote_engram.prepare_forward(False)
+        for layer_index, layer in enumerate(layers):
+            count = int(config["engram_num_embeddings"][layer_index])
+            actual = tables[layer_index].lookup(
+                base,
+                0,
+                count,
+                lambda query: torch.empty(
+                    (query.numel(), 256), dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda"
+                ),
+            )
+            torch.cuda.synchronize()
+            assert torch.equal(
+                actual.cpu().view(torch.int16),
+                references[layer_index].view(torch.int16),
+            ), layer
+            print(f"PASS noncp layer={layer} selections={base.numel()}", flush=True)
+        if reader.context.graph_replays < 2:
+            raise RuntimeError("expected a graph replay for each layer")
+        print(f"PASS graph_replays={reader.context.graph_replays}", flush=True)
+    finally:
+        if reader is not None:
+            reader.close()
+    print("PASS reader closed", flush=True)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+                "data_offsets": [0, len(weight)],
+            }
+            tensors[scale_name] = {
+                "dtype": "F8_E8M0",
+                "shape": [rows, 8],
+                "data_offsets": [len(weight), len(weight) + len(scale)],
+            }
+            weight_map[weight_name] = weight_map[scale_name] = shard
+            payloads[shard] = (weight, scale)
+        (root / "model.safetensors.index.json").write_text(
+            json.dumps({"weight_map": weight_map})
+        )
+        for shard, (weight, scale) in payloads.items():
+            write_safetensors(
+                root / shard,
+                {k: v for k, v in tensors.items() if weight_map[k] == shard},
+                weight + scale,
+            )
+        return payloads
+
+    def test_row264_matches_checkpoint_bytes_and_identity(self):
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            root = Path(tmp)
+            payloads = self.make_checkpoint(root)
+            manifest = inspect_checkpoint(root)
+            total = sum(spec["nbytes"] for spec in manifest["specs"])
+            packed_buffer = bytearray(total)
+            packed_tables, packed_samples = _copy_and_sample_row264(
+                manifest, memoryview(packed_buffer), chunk_bytes=2 * 264
+            )
+
+            self.assertEqual(
+                [(x["layer"], x["kind"]) for x in packed_tables],
+                [(1, "row264"), (14, "row264")],
+            )
+            self.assertTrue(all(x["exact_match"] for x in packed_samples))
+            self.assertEqual(
+                manifest["identity_material"],
+                inspect_checkpoint(root)["identity_material"],
+            )
+
+            offset = 0
+            for layer, rows, shard in (
+                (1, 2, "model-00047-of-00048.safetensors"),
+                (14, 3, "model-00048-of-00048.safetensors"),
+            ):
+                weight, scale = payloads[shard]
+                for row in range(rows):
+                    expected = (
+                        weight[row * 256 : (row + 1) * 256]
+                        + scale[row * 8 : (row + 1) * 8]
+                    )
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        bytes(
+                            packed_buffer[offset + row * 264 : offset + (row + 1) * 264]
+                        ),
+                        expected,
+                    )
+                offset += rows * 264
+
+            row_md = build_owner_metadata(
+                manifest,
+                packed_tables,
+                [21, 22],
+                [x["nbytes"] for x in packed_tables],
+                0,
+                55000,
+                b"native-md",
+                storage_layout="row264",
+            )
+            self.assertEqual(row_md["storage_layout"], "row264")
+            self.assertEqual(manifest["checkpoint_identity"], row_md["checkpoint_id"])
+            self.assertEqual(len(row_md["addresses"]), 2)
+            self.assertEqual(
+                [
+                    (x["layer"], x["kind"], x["rows"], x["columns"])
+                    for x in row_md["table_specs"]
+                ],
+                [(1, "row264", 2, 264), (14, "row264", 3, 264)],
+            )
+            self.assertEqual(
+                row_md["table_specs"][0]["component_layout"]["scale"]["offset"], 256
+            )
+
+    def test_row264_copy_enforces_bounded_chunk(self):
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            root = Path(tmp)
+            self.make_checkpoint(root)
+            manifest = inspect_checkpoint(root)
+            backing = bytearray(sum(spec["nbytes"] for spec in manifest["specs"]))
+            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "copy chunk"):
+                _copy_and_sample_row264(
+                    manifest, memoryview(backing), MAX_COPY_CHUNK + 1
+                )
+
+    def test_row264_metadata_rejects_wrong_mr_count_or_order(self):
+        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
+            root = Path(tmp)
+            self.make_checkpoint(root)
+            manifest = inspect_checkpoint(root)
+            tables = [
+                {
+                    "layer": 1,
+                    "kind": "row264",
+                    "nbytes": 528,
+                    "rows": 2,
+                    "columns": 264,
+                    "shape": [2, 264],
+                },
+                {
+                    "layer": 14,
+                    "kind": "row264",
+                    "nbytes": 792,
+                    "rows": 3,
+                    "columns": 264,
+                    "shape": [3, 264],
+                },
+            ]
+            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "ordered table MRs"):
+                build_owner_metadata(
+                    manifest,
+                    tables,
+                    [1, 2, 3],
+                    [528, 792, 0],
+                    0,
+                    55000,
+                    b"md",
+                    storage_layout="row264",
+                )
+            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "MR order"):
+                build_owner_metadata(
+                    manifest,
+                    list(reversed(tables)),
+                    [1, 2],
+                    [792, 528],
+                    0,
+                    55000,
+                    b"md",
+                    storage_layout="row264",
+                )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
